extraction_warnings: This paper is primarily a genomics/population-structure study; the schema (designed for curatedMetagenomicData-style sample metadata) does not map cleanly, as no sample-level or subject-level identifier table is present in the provided text.
Subgroups were constructed post hoc from the 'Experimental Model and Subject Details' paragraph (country x age-class) since the paper does not explicitly define named subgroups/subcohorts.

Age and sex values are reported as subgroup-level means/percentages, not per-subject values; some fields (e.g., sex) could not be mapped to the required single-value enum when percentages indicated mixed sex composition.
Table S1, S2, S4, S5 (referenced extensively for per-sample/per-genome metadata) were not included in the provided text, so sample_id, subject_id, and other granular fields could not be extracted.
Supplementary files provided (mmc1.pdf, mmc7.pdf) duplicate the main text/abstract rather than providing new sample-level tables.

This paper is primarily a genomic/microbiome population study; most clinical/host metadata fields (zygosity, BMI, treatment, disease response, neonatal/obgyn details, HLA, smoking, dietary restriction) are not reported for the sequenced human cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) and were marked not_reported.
Disease status ('Healthy') applies uniformly across all newly sequenced subgroups (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania adults/children/infants) per Experimental Model and Subject Details section.

Age data (age_min, age_max, age_years) are subgroup-level averages/ranges reported for adults, children, and infants within each of the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania); no per-sample age data given in main text.

Disease/case-control cohort information (CRC, T2D, IBD, hypertension, liver cirrhosis) referenced in Results for association analyses pertains to previously published external datasets, not directly characterized subjects in this paper; thus disease field was not extended to include these external disease labels for the newly generated cohort.

This paper is a microbial genomics/metagenomics study of Prevotella copri and does not contain clinical biomarker, overall survival, ECOG performance status, or tumor size data as defined by this schema.
Most schema fields are clinical/oncology-oriented and not applicable to this microbiome genomics paper; all such fields were marked not_reported.
Fecal and coprolite samples were used as source material for metagenomic sequencing, but no 'feces phenotype value' field (e.g., consistency score) was reported.

host_species was inferred as 'Human' based on extensive contextual evidence (human gut microbiome, human stool samples, human archaeological remains) rather than a single explicit statement of species name in a metadata field.
